FN-G3ZUA6C-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 227
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Representative Jim Hill
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 01/27/2026
House Bill 227 as introduced would codify the existing practice of the Administrative Office of
Courts to transfer state funds to a non-profit entity for judicial education and allow this entity to
collect nonpublic funds.
This bill would not otherwise directly affect state or local funding.

FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 227
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Representative Jim Hill
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: «Released Date»
House Bill 227 as reported by the Committee on Judiciary would decrease sales and use tax
receipts to the Education Trust Fund, by the estimated annual amounts listed below beginning in
Fiscal Year 2027 and ending in Fiscal Year 2031, based on information provided by the entity,
by exempting the Alabama Judicial College Education Fund from paying state sales and use
taxes.
This bill could also decrease sales and use tax receipts to counties and municipalities, by the
amounts listed below, provided the respective local governments adopt an exemption from local
sales and use taxes, pursuant to this bill
Education Trust Fund $28,000
County Funds $17,500
Municipal Funds $24,500
Total $70,000
Further, this bill provides that any monies received by the fund from a nonpublic source that
exceeds $2,500 are to be made public as part of the annual audit pursuant to the provisions of
this bill.
In addition, this bill provides that funds received by an entity created pursuant to the provisions
of this bill cannot be conditioned for certain judicial personnel.
